issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments, and Main (template) instantiates Farm with new Farm(). However, the reference solution only provides a Farm(int initialCapacity) constructor and no no-argument constructor. This mismatch will cause compilation errors for code that uses new Farm() and conflicts with the stated exercise requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template Main to require Farm(int initialCapacity) if the parameterized constructor is intentional. The preferred fix is to add the no-arg constructor so Main.new Farm() and the exercise instructions remain consistent.
